title: Slot-packing precision allocator for long-context KV (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Build and validate a model-specific allocator that reduces KV cache fragmentation and improves GPU memory utilization for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants while preserving continuous-batching throughput and tight P99 latency targets. The feature introduces a slot-packing allocator with mixed-precision awareness and time-decayed residency scoring. Goals: 1) reduce tail OOMs on 80k+ sequence distributions, 2) lower average GPU reserved headroom by ~12-18%, 3) keep streaming P99 latency increase <5ms for 99% of traffic. Scope: allocator logic, profiling harness, microbench suite, rollout gating, and an ops runbook. Out of scope: model architecture changes or offline quantization toolchain modifications.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler demonstrates reduction in free-list fragmentation compared to baseline for Llama-65B longctx (A40, 80k seq distribution)
End-to-end throughput with continuous batching remains within ±3% of baseline under representative traffic
P99 latency increase due to reallocation path is <5ms in 95th percentile of traces
Automated canary shows no increase in OOM incidents over a 24h window and memory headroom reduced by at least 10% on average for Mistral-70B longctx
Design doc and performance spreadsheet (per-variant) published and reviewed by runtime and infra leads
tasks: Design slot granularity and alignment rules (4-level granularity: micro, small, medium, slab)
Implement mixed-precision aware allocator that co-locates fp16/8 KV shards to minimize padding waste
Add time-decayed residency score and eviction hinting into KV manager
Integrate allocator with continuous-batching pipeline and ensure KV pin/unpin hooks are efficient
Build microbench suite that simulates Llama/Mistral/Qwen token traces (varied seq length mix)
Run GPU-level memory heatmaps and produce per-variant tuning table
Create canary rollout plan and automated gating dashboards
Author ops runbook for troubleshooting fragmentation and forced-eviction scenarios
comments: 2026-02-15 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after spike investigating frequent headroom allocations during long-context demos. Initial hypothesis: small misaligned KV shards create high fragmentation under mixed batch sizes.

2026-02-18 - Marcus Liu: Prototype allocator that groups KV shards into 64B-aligned micro-slots landed; microbench shows 6% reduction in slack for synthetic 32k traces. Need to expand to multi-precision packing.

2026-02-24 - Runtime lead (Elena Gomez): Reviewed proposal; asked to add residency decay and avoid eviction jitter that could harm streaming latency. Recommended adding per-request KV hint for short-lived prefixes.

2026-03-02 - Marcus Liu: Implemented residency scoring plus an eviction bias towards non-hot slabs. Nightly run against Llama-65B trace reduced average reserved headroom by 14% but introduced 7ms median allocation latency on cold path — investigating async prefetch strategy.

2026-03-09 - PM (Nora Chen): Prioritize Mistral-variant tuning table for customer facing demo next month. Also requested breakdown of memory wins by sequence bucket (short/medium/long).
2026-03-10 - Marcus Liu: Updated ticket with new microbench CSVs and heatmap links. Working on async prefetch to hide cold allocation cost; plan to start 10% canary next week.
rollout_plan:
Stage 0: internal perf experiments on canary cluster (dev)
Stage 1: 10% traffic canary with automated OOM/latency gating for 48h
Stage 2: 50% traffic ramp with 7-day observation window and AB metrics for cost-per-token and P99 latency
Stage 3: global rollout with auto-fallback if OOM delta or P99 jitter exceeds thresholds
runbook: Symptoms: increased OOMs, large free-list count, or sustained allocation latency spikes. Actions: 1) toggle allocator to baseline via feature-flag, 2) collect heap/kv-residency heatmap, 3) force compact operation on selected slabs, 4) escalate to runtime on-call with trace id and allocation profile
notes: Tradeoffs: tighter packing reduces reserved headroom but increases complexity of async compaction and risk of transient allocation latency. Chosen default: conservative slot coalescing for production; aggressive mode behind feature flag for experimental clusters. We may iterate packing thresholds per-variant (LLAMA-65B vs QWEN-54B) based on measured live distributions.
